title: Negative possession with singular owners
focus: Build singular-owner negative possession statements: owner + ei ole + partitive thing.
prerequisiteSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession

exercises.prompt: Repair “Hänellä eivät ole palloa.” to mean “He does not have a ball.” Use hänellä ("he as owner") and palloa ("ball").
exercises.explanation: Possession uses fixed ei ole with every owner, not personal negative-verb agreement.
requiredSkills: Regular singular partitive in negative possession
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Negative possession sentences: form or meaning confused

sentenceExplanation.translation: He does not have a ball.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed ei ole + singular partitive noun

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: hän has the learned possession form hänellä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Possession uses fixed ei with minulla, sinulla and hänellä; do not change it to en or et.
After ei, olla uses ole. Together ei ole means “do not have” or “does not have” here.
pallo + -a = palloa. This is the singular partitive, the noun form used when possession is denied.
